newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 6.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 6.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Monday:

* President Suharto will deliver to parliament on Monday Indonesia's budget for the year from April 1997 to March 1998. Suharto's speech starts around 0300 GMT and economists say he is expected to announce a moderate expansion of the budget to sustain annual economic growth of just over seven percent.
* Indonesia's central bank, Bank Indonesia, said on Friday it had cut its bill of exchange discount rates by between one and 1.5 percent to stimulate exports.

* The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 101.60 points, or 1.6 percent, to close at 6,544.09 on Friday amid new optimism about the U.S. economy and an improving outlook for semiconductor companies. It was one of its biggest point gains ever.
* Indonesia's government is upbeat that the country's unhusked rice production would meet the target of 52.19 million tonnes in 1997, despite some areas suffering drought.
* The Jakarta Composite index rose 8.09 points, or 1.27 percent, to close at 646.19 points on Friday following a late spurt of buying in selected big-capitalised stocks.
* On Monday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,361.75/62.10 in early trading against the opening of 2,361.80/62.80.
* Telkom following the government's decision to revise local telephone tariffs.
* Indosat on the announcement it plans to spend 490 billion rupiah in 1997 on an expansion programme to boost net profit.
* Property firm Summarecon on market talk that the firm is likely to acquire another property firm and announce a rights issue.
* Timber firms Barito and Sumalindo on reports of increased Indonesian forestry exports in 1996.
